correctness.rationale: All divisors of squarefree pqr are explicit. The largest-prime congruence yields pq-1=kr with 1<=k<p. The middle-prime condition forces pr≡1 mod q and hence q=p+k. Mod p gives qr≡-1; for odd p, q cannot be 1 mod p, so r≡1 mod p forces k=p-1 and (q,r)=(2p-1,2p+1). Mod 3 restricts odd p to 3; p=2 yields (2,3,5). Both final witness sets were checked exactly. The one- and two-support exclusions are direct. A standalone exhaustive direct divisor checker tested 776216 triples with prime factors below 1000 and a separate 100000 prime-shape range, finite only.

value.rationale: The exact classification closes the first nonempty squarefree prime-support stratum of the numerical Sylow necessary condition, a classical object whose complete-set density was determined in 2026. It identifies precisely the two sizes 30 and 105 for which the numerical test alone fails to rule out a hypothetical nonabelian simple group among all squarefree orders with at most three prime supports, while the group-theoretic theorem rules those groups out. The claim is a natural complete infinite classification, not the recomputation of two known listed values; the primitive congruence rigidity is transferable to other small-support divisor-witness problems.
